title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: available in the US Department of Defense (DoD) cloud
summary: Hold: the page incorrectly says every admin-centre step requires the AI administrator role, including licence assignment. Microsoft requires at least a License or User Administrator for licence assignment; the roadmap facts and connector controls otherwise have supporting documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-07-13T23:07:14.
Connectors integrate content from external data sources into Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Copilot connectors enable organizations to integrate content from  other external data sources into Microsoft Graph, improving Copilot’s intelligence, contextual responses, and content discoverability

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Connector content can be searched and used for reasoning in Copilot and Microsoft Search.
claims.quote: Synced and federated connectors power Microsoft 365 Copilot and other Microsoft 365 intelligent experiences, such as Microsoft Search, Copilot in Excel, and the Researcher agent.

claims.claim: The connectors overview lists commercial, GCC, GCC High and DoD availability.
claims.quote: Copilot connectors are available in commercial environments and in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud (GCC), Government Community Cloud High (GCCH), and Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot service description marks Microsoft 365 Copilot Connectors as available in DoD.
claims.quote: | Feature | Commercial/Worldwide | GCC | GCCH | DoD | ... | Microsoft 365 Copilot Connectors | Yes | Yes^9^ | Yes^9^ | Yes^9^ |

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Synced connectors index external content on a recurring schedule.
claims.quote: Synced connectors index content from an external data source into the Microsoft 365 substrate on a recurring schedule.

claims.claim: Federated connectors query external content in real time through MCP without indexing it into Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Federated connectors retrieve content in real time by using Model Context Protocol (MCP) without indexing data into Microsoft Graph.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: External connections and partner connectors are off by default in government clouds, so leaving them unconfigured does not start indexing.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Connectors: External connections and partner connectors aren't enabled by default for government clouds.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The service description does not give a government-cloud enablement procedure or a separate tenant-enablement switch supplied by the listed connection and ACL controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors DoD government cloud enable external connections partner connectors switch. Read service description, deployment-overview and federated-connectors-overview; no government-specific enablement procedure found.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Configuring and deploying Copilot connectors requires an AI administrator in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: To configure and deploy Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Prebuilt synced connectors require admin access to the external service.
claims.quote: In addition, for prebuilt synced connectors (such as Google Drive, Confluence, ServiceNow), you must have admin access to the external service (Google Workspace Super Admin, Confluence Admin).

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Administrators can deploy a connector to a subset of users for validation before wider rollout.
claims.quote: Deploy the connector to a subset of users for validation before a broader rollout.

claims.claim: Create deploys the connection and starts indexing with default settings.
claims.quote: Choose Create to deploy the connection. The connector begins indexing content using default settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Connectors > Gallery > data source reaches connector setup.
claims.quote: In the left pane, choose Copilot > Connectors. On the Connectors tab, in the left pane, choose Gallery, and select the data source you want to connect ... Choose Create to deploy the connection.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Copilot > Connectors > Connectors > Gallery > data source > Create'. The printed route reaches the correct setup page but stops before the deployment control; credentials and other fields remain part of the linked procedure.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/external/connections creates a connection for custom connectors.
claims.quote: Create a new externalConnection object. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections

claims.claim: Copilot > Connectors > Connectors > Gallery > data source > Custom setup > Users > Access Permissions reaches the gallery connector visibility setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: On the connector page in the admin center, select Custom setup. ... On the Users tab, under Access Permissions, choose whether indexed data is visible to: Only users with access to the content; Everyone in the organization

claims.claim: PUT /v1.0/external/connections/{connection-id}/items/{item-id} creates a custom connector item whose acl property sets its access control list.
claims.quote: PUT https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr/items/TSP228082938 ... acl | microsoft.graph.externalConnectors.acl collection | The access control list. Required.

claims.claim: Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses reaches user licence assignment in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user ... In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a user licence through Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: All admin-centre steps, including user licence assignment, need the AI administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.
claims.fix: Replace 'All admin-centre steps need the AI administrator role.' with 'Connector deployment and gallery access configuration require the AI administrator role. Assigning user licences requires at least a License or User Administrator.' The licence-assignment source already cited gives the latter requirement.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Imported and indexed connector content is Customer Data in the organisation's Microsoft 365 services.
claims.quote: Data imported into your Microsoft 365 services using Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors will be "Customer Data" under the Product Terms, Data Protection Addendum, and Microsoft's enterprise data obligations.

claims.claim: The organisation is responsible as data controller for connector functionality and compliance with third-party obligations.
claims.quote: As the data controller, you're solely and exclusively responsible for: a) the Connector Functionality; and b) using the Microsoft 365 Copilot connector in compliance with any third-party rights, licenses, and obligations.

claims.claim: Connector use may be subject to third-party terms and conditions.
claims.quote: The use of Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors may be subject to third-party terms and conditions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[1]
claims.claim: Access Permissions can expose indexed connector data to everyone in the organisation or restrict it to users with access to the content.
claims.quote: On the Users tab, under Access Permissions, choose whether indexed data is visible to: Only users with access to the content; Everyone in the organization

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Item access permissions govern what connector content users can see in Copilot and Search.
claims.quote: Each item includes content, metadata (like title and URL), and an access control list (ACL) that enforces permissions. ... Search and Copilot only show items to users who have access in the source system.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview to sources for the statement that connector item permissions are enforced in both Search and Copilot.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Incremental crawls do not process permission updates.
claims.quote: Incremental crawls don't support permission updates. Run full crawls periodically to maintain sync accuracy.

claims.claim: A source permission removal is reflected through a full crawl rather than an incremental crawl.
claims.quote: Use a full refresh in scenarios such as: ... Updating ACLs. ... Incremental crawls don't currently process updates to permissions.

claims.claim: Synced connectors require data source credentials, such as API keys or service account tokens.
claims.quote: Data source authentication credentials, such as API keys or service account tokens.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Default identity mapping matches email to UserPrincipalName or Mail in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: By default, the system maps users by matching their email to UserPrincipalName or Mail in Microsoft Entra ID. In the Map Identities section, you can provide a custom mapping formula.

claims.claim: The published usdodcentral IPv4 range is 57.17.40.192/26.
The published usdodeast IPv4 range is 52.181.74.64/26.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Sources using IP firewall rules need to allow the connector service's relevant published ranges.
claims.quote: If your data source uses IP firewall rules, allow access to the Copilot connectors service by permitting the following IP ranges.

claims.claim: Synced connector ingestion reads and indexes content rather than writing changes to the source system.
claims.quote: | Connectors | Plugins | ... | Run on a schedule | Run in real-time | ... | One way data flow (read) | Can support two-way data flow (read and write) |
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/compliance/anz/blueprint-copilot-servicecom to sources for the scheduled, one-way read behaviour of synced connectors; retain the existing qualification about broader connector functionality in the terms of use.

claims.claim: Enabling connectors can authorise sending Customer Data to third-party services, subject to configuration.
claims.quote: By enabling Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors, you authorize Microsoft to, subject to your configurations: ... 2) send your Customer Data and Personal Data ... to third-party services

claims.claim: Enabling connectors can authorise modifying data in third-party services, subject to configuration.
claims.quote: By enabling Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors, you authorize Microsoft to, subject to your configurations: ... 4) modify data in third-party services
